steps.title: Grow cells to confluency
steps.instruction: Culture the chosen cancer cell line in appropriate medium at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until ~80 % confluency is reached; aim for 5 × 10⁷–1 × 10⁹ cells per preparation.

steps.title: Harvest cells under hypoxia or normoxia
steps.instruction: Collect cells according to the oxygen condition, keeping all steps for hypoxic samples inside the hypoxia chamber.

substeps.instruction: Hypoxic samples:
a. Pre‑equilibrate PBS and collection tubes in the hypoxia chamber overnight.
b. Remove medium and wash cells twice with PBS (cold).
c. Detach cells with a cell scraper in PBS.
d. Transfer suspension to 15 mL or 50 mL conical tubes and centrifuge 500 × g, 5 min, 4 °C; keep tubes in the chamber.
e. Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in PBS, repeat centrifugation, discard supernatant.
f. Use the pellet directly for HLA‑I profiling or snap‑freeze in liquid N₂ for later use.
Normoxic samples:
a. Transfer cells to 15 mL or 50 mL conical tubes, centrifuge 500 × g, 5 min, 4 °C.
b. Discard supernatant, wash cells twice with cold PBS, discard supernatant.
c. Use the pellet directly for HLA‑I profiling or snap‑freeze; dry pellets may be stored at –80 °C up to 6 months.

steps.title: Prepare all buffers and reagents
steps.instruction: Make the solutions listed in the Recipes section fresh before use; keep them cold.

substeps.instruction: Boric acid‑KCl stock (0.1 M each): dissolve 0.62 g boric acid and 0.75 g KCl in LC‑MS‑grade water to 100 mL.
Borate wash buffer (0.1 M NaOH, 0.1 M boric acid‑KCl): mix 4 mL 0.1 M NaOH, 50 mL boric acid‑KCl stock, 100 mL water.
Dimethyl pimelimidate (DMP) 40 mM: dissolve 250 mg DMP in 8 mL borate wash buffer, adjust pH to 9.0 with 1 M NaOH, bring to 25 mL with borate wash buffer (prepare fresh).
Termination buffer (0.2 M Tris, pH 8.0): mix 20 mL 1 M Tris stock with 80 mL water.

2× Lysis buffer: 10 mL 100 mM Tris pH 8.0 (from 1 M Tris), 20 mL 300 mM NaCl (from 1.5 M NaCl), 10 mL 1 % IGEPAL (from 10 % stock), 60 mL water; add one protease‑inhibitor tablet per 10 mL (and PhosStop if needed) just before use; keep cold.
Wash buffer 1 (50 mM Tris pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl, 5 mM EDTA): 5 mL 1 M Tris, 10 mL 1.5 M NaCl, 1 mL 0.5 M EDTA, 84 mL water.
Wash buffer 2 (50 mM Tris pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl): 5 mL 1 M Tris, 10 mL 1.5 M NaCl, 85 mL water.
Wash buffer 3 (50 mM Tris pH 8.0, 450 mM NaCl): 5 mL 1 M Tris, 30 mL 1.5 M NaCl, 65 mL water.
Wash buffer 4 (50 mM Tris pH 8.0 only): 5 mL 1 M Tris, 95 mL water.
10 % (v/v) acetic acid: 25 mL glacial acetic acid + 225 mL water.
1 M NaOH: dissolve 4 g NaOH in 100 mL water.
0.1 M NaOH: dissolve 0.4 g NaOH in 100 mL water.
1 M Tris pH 8.0: dissolve 121.14 g Tris in 800 mL water, adjust pH to 8.0 with ~42 mL HCl.
20 % ACN 0.1 % TFA: 10 mL ACN + 50 µL TFA + 39.95 mL water.
80 % ACN 0.1 % TFA: 40 mL ACN + 50 µL TFA + water to 50 mL.
50 % ACN 0.1 % TFA: 25 mL ACN + 50 µL TFA + water to 50 mL.
1 % ACN 0.1 % TFA: 500 µL ACN + 50 µL TFA + 49.45 mL water.
0.1 % TFA: 50 µL TFA + 49.45 mL water.
Mass‑spec loading buffer: 500 µL ACN + 50 µL 0.1 % formic acid + 49.45 mL water.

steps.title: Prepare cross‑linked protein A beads
steps.instruction: Wash, couple antibody, cross‑link, quench, and store the immuno‑resin.

substeps.instruction: Wash column: incubate resin in 10 % acetic acid for ≥30 min, then wash thoroughly with PBS until pH is neutral (check with pH strip).

Resuspend protein A Sepharose (50 % w/v slurry in 20 % ethanol) by gentle inversion; transfer required volume (≈50 µL dry beads per 1 mg antibody) to a 50 mL tube, fill with PBS, centrifuge 100 × g, 1 min, discard ethanol supernatant.
Antibody coupling: dilute monoclonal anti‑HLA‑I (clone W6/32) to 0.5–1 mg mL⁻¹ in PBS, add to washed beads, rotate at ~11 rpm, RT for 30 min (or 1–4 h at 4 °C).
Remove residual primary amines: wash resin with 10 column volumes (CV) of borate wash buffer; do not let resin dry.
Cross‑link: add 10 CV of freshly prepared 40 mM DMP solution, let buffer drain to just above resin bed, seal bottom, incubate 30 min at RT.
Quench: wash beads with 10 CV ice‑cold 0.2 M Tris pH 8.0.
Neutralize: wash with 10 CV termination buffer (50 mM Tris pH 8.0) and confirm neutral pH.
Recover resin: gently resuspend beads with a 10 mL stripette, transfer to a clean container containing 50 mM Tris pH 8.0; store at 4 °C up to 1 month.

steps.title: Generate cell lysate and clarify
steps.instruction: Lyse cells, remove nuclei and debris, and normalize protein concentration.

substeps.instruction: Thaw cell pellets on ice.
Add ~0.5 mL ice‑cold 2× lysis buffer per sample; pipette gently with low‑retention tips until homogeneous; add more buffer if needed for complete resuspension.
Rotate lysate at 4 °C for 30 min (do not exceed).
Centrifuge 500 × g, 15 min, 4 °C to pellet nuclei; collect supernatant, freeze nuclear pellet at –80 °C if desired.
Clarify: transfer supernatant to pre‑chilled 2 mL LoBind tube, centrifuge 20 000 × g, 45 min, 4 °C.
Optional: determine protein concentration with Pierce BCA kit; if needed, dilute all samples to the lowest measured concentration using 50 mM Tris pH 8.0 so that final lysis buffer is 1×.

steps.title: Immunoprecipitate MHC‑I complexes
steps.instruction: Incubate clarified lysate with cross‑linked protein A resin to capture MHC‑peptide complexes.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot required volume of cross‑linked resin into 2 mL LoBind tubes (e.g., 20 µL dry beads per 0.5–2 mL lysate).
Add clarified lysate to beads (recommended 0.5–2 mL lysate per 20 µL dry beads).
Incubate overnight (12–16 h) at 4 °C on an orbital rotator (~10–15 rpm).
If lysate volume >2 mL, split across multiple tubes to maintain bead‑lysate contact.

steps.title: Wash and elute MHC‑peptide complexes
steps.instruction: Remove contaminants with sequential washes and elute bound peptides with acidic buffer.

substeps.instruction: Re‑condition column: incubate with 10 % acetic acid for 30 min, then wash with PBS; verify neutral pH.
Load lysate onto the column containing the immuno‑resin; collect flowthrough in labeled tubes and store at –80 °C (optional for MHC‑II IP).
Wash resin sequentially with ≥10 CV of each wash buffer:
a. Wash buffer 1 (low‑salt, chelating).
b. Wash buffer 2 (low‑salt).
c. Wash buffer 3 (high‑salt).
d. Wash buffer 4 (very low‑salt).
Do not let resin dry between washes.
Elute complexes: add 5 CV of 10 % acetic acid, collect eluate into LoBind 2 mL tubes; use a syringe plunger to push remaining liquid through.

steps.title: Separate peptides from MHC complexes (filter)
steps.instruction: Use ultrafree‑MC centrifugal filter units to collect peptides and wash the membrane.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑condition each filter with 500 µL 10 % acetic acid; centrifuge 15 000 × g, 45–60 min, 4 °C.
Discard flowthrough, rinse filter bottom with 500 µL 10 % acetic acid (pipette up/down).
Load the acid eluate onto the pre‑conditioned filter; centrifuge 15 000 × g, ~1 h, 4 °C (or split into batches if volume exceeds capacity).
Collect filtrate in low‑binding tubes; add 50 µL 20 % ACN 0.1 % TFA onto the membrane, centrifuge 15 000 × g, 30 min, 4 °C to recover residual peptides.
Combine the wash with the main filtrate, then dry combined eluate in a Speed‑Vac; store dried peptides at –20 °C (pause point).

steps.title: Desalt peptides with C18 spin tips
steps.instruction: Condition, equilibrate, load, wash and elute peptides using Pierce C18 96‑tip plates.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend dried peptides in 50 µL 1 % ACN 0.1 % TFA; verify pH < 4 with strip.
Shake on orbital shaker at 1 000 × g for 10–15 min (IKA VX 2E.n).
Sonicate 3–5 min in water bath (no temperature control).
Centrifuge 20 000 × g, 10 min, 4 °C; keep supernatant.
Insert each C18 tip into spin adapter inside a clean 2 mL tube.
Condition tip: add 20 µL 80 % ACN 0.1 % TFA, centrifuge 1 000 × g, 1 min.
Equilibrate twice: add 20 µL 0.1 % TFA, centrifuge 1 min each time; discard flowthrough.
Load 20–50 µL peptide solution onto tip, centrifuge 1 min at 1 000 × g (extend to 2–3 min if flow is slow).
Wash tip twice with 20 µL 0.1 % TFA, centrifuge 1 min each.
Transfer tip to a new tube, elute twice with 20 µL 50 % ACN 0.1 % TFA, centrifuge 1 min each.
Pool eluates, dry in Speed‑Vac (avoid complete dryness).
Store partially dried peptides at –80 °C or proceed immediately to LC‑MS/MS.

steps.title: Prepare samples for LC‑MS/MS
steps.instruction: Resuspend peptides, remove particulates, and load onto the mass spectrometer.

substeps.instruction: Add 15–25 µL 0.1 % formic acid to each dried peptide sample; vortex briefly.
Sonicate in water bath for 5 min.
Centrifuge 13 000 × g, 10 min, 4 °C; transfer clear supernatant to low‑bind autosampler vials, avoiding bubbles.
Inject onto LC‑MS/MS system (e.g., Thermo Fisher Q‑Exactive‑HF) using the gradient and settings listed in Table 2.

steps.title: LC‑MS/MS acquisition settings
steps.instruction: Run the instrument with the following parameters: spray voltage 1 700–2 200 V, capillary temperature 275 °C, MS1 300–1800 m/z at 70 000 resolution, ion target 5 × 10⁵, max injection 120 ms; select top 20 precursors per cycle (charge 2–4+), HCD 27 %, MS2 resolution 35 000, ion target 1 × 10⁵, isolation width 1.2 Da, underfill 1 %, dynamic exclusion 15 s.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol has been used and validated in the following research article: • Estephan et al. [28]. Hypoxia promotes tumor immune evasion by suppressing MHC-I expression and antigen presentation. EMBO Journal (Figures 5B–E and 6 and Supplementary Figures 6, 7, and 9).
